item.title: Re: 9th Annual Holiday Art Exchange~!
item.content:encoded:
I got double the gifts for double the Art Exchange! :D

The first one I got was: http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/kirbgift

It's a very cute little tale about my smol cactus child reeking absolute havoc among civilians, GAW, and Fifthists. It's very cute and very wholesome, which is very poky energy.

The second one I got is: http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/2020ge2

This one I believe is based on SCP-4558 and Pink Cracks In A Digital Wall. It's a short little piece that makes pretty clever use of the coding syntax. I'm not sure what language it's based on if any language in particular, but it's a very clever and neat little piece exploring sermons and baptisms through code.

Thanks to whoever made these! :D

item.title: THE GREAT REVIEW
item.content:encoded:
Last year, I read (slash viewed [slash experienced]) every art exchange gift and reviewed them. I think I would like to do that once again. This forum post will be edited over the coming days to start cataloguing and commenting on every single art exchange piece. That's right!

For convenience, this will be organized by the alphabetical order of the recipient. So, when this post gets edited, the new additions may not necessarily be at the bottom. Also, I am writing this at a rather busy time, so it will take a bit for this to really start filling up. But, anyhow… here we go!

JakdragonX's gift
Life Like a Box of Chocolates

This is art of SCP-5346, which I admittedly have never read. Nonetheless, it looks like it was painted on actual canvas (that or they have a digital art filter that does that, either way it looks cool) and the eye, the hands, and the… whatever is covering where "is" should be in this saying… it looks hella neat! Wonderful gift.

item.title: Re: 9th Annual Holiday Art Exchange~!

item.title: Re: 9th Annual Holiday Art Exchange~!
item.content:encoded:
Well! Two excellent tales came my way. The first was an very nicely done character study about a survivor of SCP-4841, which really captured the melancholic loss of the thing in wonderful detail, so thank you very much!

The second was based on the WAN/Fifthism contest entries Kirby and I made a while ago, which nailed the voice and the atmosphere we were going for - thank you very much for that also!

item.title: Re: 9th Annual Holiday Art Exchange~!
item.content:encoded:
My gift can be found here: http://topia.wikidot.com/art-exchange-gift-for-uncertaintycrossing

First off, mysterious gifter, please post this to WL. please lmao. The way you expanded upon both the lore presented in the Archives and just like.. Library worldbuilding in general is really spectacular, and I know everyone else in the Library would love to see it haha.

Secondly, fucking hell I absolutely love what you've done with my little asshole of a canine. The dialogue killed me and I definitely think you nailed his personality. Just the right mix of mean old bastard with too fucking clever for his own good. Also love the take on the Gatekeeper too!! You did well with him!!

In short, thank you very much!! I'm glad your finals went well and I hope you have a wonderful rest of your holiday season!

item.title: Re: 9th Annual Holiday Art Exchange~!
item.content:encoded:
My gift, an article that covers the life and times of Lyle Burnley in the context of Fifthism and the anticolonial struggle in Vietnam, with a heaping side of anarchist theory. I have to admit that most of the request was me being quite self-indulgent, and I only expected the author to choose the Burnley thing.

But the mad lad/y actually did it! And it's great, too! Like, really, really, great, and people should read it. Thank you, Secret Santa!
